title: Population characteristics
competency: Describe age and sex structure and calculate sex ratio and age dependency ratio.

keywords.def: The distribution of a population into age groups.
A graph of the age distribution of a population by sex.
Dependent people (0–14 and 65+) per 100 working-age people (15–64).

ideas.name: Age structure and the population pyramid

en.text: Population structure has biological parts (race, ethnicity, sex, age) and cultural parts (education, health, nutrition, religion, occupation). Age groups are young 0–14, working 15–64 and old 65+. A population pyramid shows age by sex. Ethiopia's pyramid has a very broad base: many young people.

screens.title: Read the shape
screens.ask: Ethiopia's population pyramid has a very wide bottom. What does that tell us?
opts: There are more men than women
screens.after: The bottom bars are the youngest age groups. A wide base means many children and young people.

screens.title: 2.2.2 Population characteristics
paras: The structure of a population is how males and females spread over age groups.
Biological characteristics: race, ethnicity, sex and age.
Cultural characteristics: education, health, nutrition, religion and occupation.

screens.title: Age structure
paras: Age structure is the distribution of a population into age groups.
Two tools help us understand it: age groups and the population pyramid.

screens.title: Population pyramid
paras: A population pyramid is a graph of the age distribution of a population by sex.
Males are on the left, females on the right. The youngest group is at the bottom.
Pyramids of developing countries like Ethiopia have very broad bases. Young people dominate.
screens.note: Figure 2.3: Ethiopia, 2007. The widest bars are ages 5–9; the bars get thinner towards the top.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The distribution of a population into age groups.
A graph of the age distribution of a population by sex.

screens.text: The graph of the age distribution of a population by sex is called…
screens.why: A population pyramid is that graph.
screens.clue: It is a picture with bars, shaped like a triangle.

screens.why: Biological: race, ethnicity, sex, age. Cultural: education, health, nutrition, religion, occupation.
screens.clue: Is it something you are born with, or something you learn or do?

screens.text: A 70-year-old grandmother belongs to which age group?
Country P's pyramid is narrow at the bottom and wide in the middle. Compared with Ethiopia it has…
screens.why: The bottom bars are the young. A narrow base means a smaller share of children than Ethiopia's broad base.
screens.clue: What do the bottom bars stand for?

ideas.name: Sex ratio and age dependency ratio

en.text: Sex ratio is the number of males for every 100 females: (male ÷ female) × 100. Age dependency ratio compares dependents (0–14 and 65+) with the working age group (15–64), times 100. Ethiopia's dependency ratio is very high.

screens.title: Boys and girls
screens.ask: A class has 20 boys and 20 girls. How many boys are there for every 100 girls?
screens.after: Equal numbers give 100 boys per 100 girls. That number is the sex ratio.

screens.title: Sex structure
paras: Sex ratio is the ratio of the male population to the female population.
It is usually given as males per 100 females.

screens.title: Find a sex ratio
steps: Activity 2.4 Q1: a school has 3,000 students; 1,650 are female.
So there are about 82 males for every 100 females.

screens.title: Age dependency ratio
paras: Age dependency ratio (ADR) relates the working population to the non-working population.
ADR = (people aged 0–14 + people aged 65+) ÷ people aged 15–64 × 100.
In Ethiopia the ADR is very high. The burden of the young and old on workers is heavy.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Dependent people (0–14 and 65+) per 100 working-age people (15–64).

screens.ask: A village has 4,800 males and 5,000 females. Sex ratio = (4,800 ÷ 5,000) × 100 = ___
A school has 3,000 students; 1,650 are female. Sex ratio ≈ ___ (one decimal place).
screens.clue: Find the number of males first.

screens.ask: Region A: 12,191,000 under 15; 5,127,000 over 64; 29,120,000 aged 15–64. ADR ≈ ___ % (one decimal place).
screens.clue: Add the two dependent groups, divide by workers, × 100.

screens.ask: A town has 3,000 children (0–14), 1,000 old people (65+) and 5,000 people aged 15–64. ADR = ___ %

test.text: Ethiopia's population pyramid has a very broad base.
Which is a cultural characteristic of a population?
test.why: Cultural: education, health, nutrition, religion, occupation.
